bull_thesis:
KBR splits in two on 4 January 2027, seven weeks from now, and after a 9% two-day fall around its investor days the shares at $35.67 (16 November 2026) already price the outcome in which the split happens and nobody re-rates either half. The event is firmer than a week ago: both companies restated the 4 January date at their own investor days on 11 and 12 November 2026, Trinzic's chief executive called it "on track," the registration statement every American spin-off must file (a Form 10) was amended on 9 November, the eight-person Trinzic board is named, and standalone systems are live.

The retained KBR is the half worth owning. It keeps the process-technology and advisory business - about $2.90 billion of 2026 revenue at a 14.7% margin on a fully loaded standalone basis - and targets 10% or more organic revenue growth a year to 2029, a 12% or better adjusted margin on earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (adjusted EBITDA), and 85% or better free cash flow conversion. Its 2027 adjusted EBITDA target is more than $425 million even after absorbing a roughly $100 million fall in joint-venture income, which means the core is growing faster than the headline. It leaves with net leverage below two times and plans to sell its 19.9% Trinzic stake within about twelve months to take leverage below about one times.

The parts, at ordinary multiples, are worth about $46 a KBR share: Trinzic at 8.0 times its $483 million of trailing adjusted EBITDA, less about $1.52 billion of net debt, is about $18.60 a share; retained KBR at 10.0 times $425 million, less about $0.85 billion of net debt, is about $27.00. That is roughly 29% above today. The conditions: the board declares the distribution and sets a record date in December, Trinzic's roughly $1.7 billion of borrowing prices without a punitive coupon, and the two halves trade near their own peer groups once separated rather than at the bottom of them.
bear_thesis:
A fixed date is not a fixed payout. A spin-off is not a takeover: there is no offer, no counterparty and no contractual price, only a hope that two securities are valued more generously apart than together. The investor days were the information event that was supposed to prove that hope, and the market marked the stock down 9% in two days on what it heard.

The disclosed numbers were weaker than the street had assumed. Retained KBR's standalone earning power is about $425 million of adjusted EBITDA once it carries $107 million of allocated corporate and shared cost - not the $460-500 million many parts valuations used - and a liquefied-natural-gas joint venture worth about $100 million a year is winding down. Trinzic launches at about 3.15 times net leverage with revenue facing a roughly $200 million (4%) NASA insourcing headwind in 2027, 83% federal revenue, management calling 2027 "a modest growth year," and a government-services peer group whose multiples have fallen from about 13 times in mid-2024 to about 9 times.

Everything that makes the split legally happen is still open seven weeks out: the record date, the distribution ratio and the financing amounts are blank in the amended Form 10, no condition has been satisfied, and KBR "has the right to terminate or modify the distribution, even if all of the conditions are satisfied." The company has already missed one separation timetable (the original "mid-to-late 2026").

Even on time, holders get Trinzic shares they did not choose into predictable forced selling, and KBR itself now plans to sell its 19.9% Trinzic stake within about twelve months - a known block of supply over the new shares. If neither half re-rates, the parts are worth about $35, roughly today's price: Trinzic at 7 times (about $14.75 a share) plus retained KBR at 8 times (about $20.20). If the split slips or is pulled, the conglomerate at 6.0-6.5 times guided 2026 earnings is worth about $33. What would confirm the bear case: no record date by about 18 December 2026, a Trinzic debt offering that prices wide or is postponed, or 2027 guidance in February below the investor-day frameworks.
sop_bull:
Event-win value about $56 a share, on a full re-rating of both halves. Share count is 126.1 million; the whole of Trinzic's equity accrues to KBR holders, 80.1% by direct distribution and 19.9% through the stake KBR will sell to repay debt, so both parts are expressed per KBR share and the stake is not counted twice.

Trinzic: 9.0 times $483 million of last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA (disclosed at its 12 November 2026 investor day) is a $4.35 billion enterprise value; less about $1.52 billion of net debt (3.15 times net leverage at separation, consistent with the Form 10's $1.705 billion of pro-forma borrowing less $200 million of cash) leaves about $2.83 billion of equity, or about $22.40 a KBR share. 9.0 times is the upper half of today's government-services range and is earned if Trinzic delivers its 9%-plus margin and 3-6% growth framework.

Retained KBR: 12.0 times about $425 million of standalone adjusted EBITDA (the investor-day baseline and the 2027 floor target) is a $5.10 billion enterprise value; less about $0.85 billion of net debt (below two times at separation) leaves about $4.25 billion, or about $33.70 a share. 12.0 times is what a licensing-heavy engineering business growing 10% a year at a 12%-plus margin and 85% cash conversion would earn once it proves it.

Together about $56.10. The catalyst board's $53 target sits just under this full re-rating case.
sop_bear:
The downside floor is about $33 a share, and it is an operating-value floor, not a contractual one. If the separation slips or is cancelled, a holder owns the conglomerate as it stands: guided 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $980 million to $1.04 billion ($1.01 billion midpoint) at 6.0-6.5 times gives a $6.06-6.57 billion enterprise value; less $2.118 billion of net debt (total debt $2.541 billion less $439 million of cash at 2 October 2026) leaves $3.94-4.45 billion of equity, or $31.30-35.30 across 126.1 million shares. Call it $33.

Corroboration: today's price implies about 6.55 times (enterprise value about $6.62 billion), so the bundle already trades at the top of that floor range; four insiders bought in the open market in May 2026 between $30.60 and $32.47; the 52-week low is $29.94, which is the stress case.

A second, higher adverse case applies if the split happens but neither half re-rates: Trinzic at 7.0 times $483 million less $1.52 billion of net debt (about $14.75 a share) plus retained KBR at 8.0 times $425 million less $0.85 billion (about $20.20) gives about $35 - essentially today's price. Below $33 needs an operating break (a lost major programme, an adverse ruling on protested awards) or a credit event; neither is visible, with about $1.1 billion of liquidity and group net leverage of 2.1 times.
sop_breakdown:
Base case about $40 a share (range $39-42), from weighting outcomes rather than picking one.

Probability the separation completes on or near 4 January 2027: about 88%, up from 85% last week because both investor days restated the date and the leadership teams presented as separate companies; it is not higher because the record date, ratio and financing are still blank and no condition has been satisfied. Conditional on completion: about 45% the halves re-rate toward the roughly $46 parts value within six to nine months, about 30% a partial re-rating to about $40, and about 25% no re-rating, about $35. That conditional value is about $41.45. The remaining 12% is a slip or cancellation back to the roughly $33 conglomerate floor. Weighted: 0.88 x $41.45 + 0.12 x $33 = about $40.40.

The roughly $46 parts value per KBR share (126.1 million shares): Trinzic at 8.0 times $483 million = $3.86 billion enterprise value, less about $1.52 billion net debt = about $2.34 billion, or $18.60; retained KBR at 10.0 times $425 million = $4.25 billion, less about $0.85 billion net debt = about $3.40 billion, or $27.00. Together about $45.60.

Inputs and where they come from. Trinzic's $483 million trailing adjusted EBITDA and 3.15 times net leverage at separation are from its 12 November 2026 investor-day materials. Retained KBR's $425 million standalone baseline (segment roughly $550 million less $107 million of corporate and shared cost and an $18 million pension item) and its below-two-times net leverage at separation are from the 11 November 2026 KBR investor-day materials; $0.85 billion is two times $425 million, a conservative ceiling. Last week's $51 parts value used about $460 million for retained KBR and about $490 million for Trinzic; the published figures are lower, which moves the parts value down by about $5 and is the honest reason the target falls from $51 to $46.
risk_reward:
About 3.9 to 1 on the parts target, and better than last week's 2.2 to 1 because the price fell further than the parts value did. From $35.67 (16 November 2026), upside to the roughly $46 parts value is about 29%, or $10.33 a share, against downside to the roughly $33 conglomerate floor of about 7.5%, or $2.67 a share. To the $40 probability-weighted base case the upside is about 12%. Measured to the 52-week low of $29.94 as a stress case the ratio is about 1.8 to 1. Against the catalyst board's stale $53 target and $33.20 floor it reads about 7 to 1, which overstates the case because the board's valuation predates the standalone disclosures.

The qualifier: the denominator is a judgement about the conglomerate multiple, not cash and not deal terms, and the price now sits right on the "split happens, no re-rating" value of about $35 - so most of the remaining downside is the slip-or-cancel path, and most of the upside depends on the two halves being priced by their own peer groups after 4 January.
catalyst_summary: Tax-free spin-off of KBR's government-services arm as Trinzic (NYSE: TZIC) firmly dated for 4 January 2027 and restated at both 11-12 November 2026 investor days; after a 9% sell-off on the standalone numbers, $35.67 sits on the no-re-rate value with about 29% upside to a $46 parts value against about 7.5% downside to a $33 conglomerate floor (about 3.9 to 1).
dated_milestone: 4 January 2027 - targeted completion of the Trinzic separation, restated by KBR at its investor day on 11 November 2026 and by Trinzic at its investor day on 12 November 2026 (Trinzic's chief executive: "on track"), subject to final KBR board approval and customary conditions. Verified chronology: announced 24 September 2025 as "Expected to be Completed Mid-to-Late 2026"; chief financial officer designate Nicholas Veasey 1 July 2026; name Trinzic 30 July 2026; 4 January 2027 date set August 2026 and unchanged since; chief executive designate Michael LaRouche 24 September 2026; Form 10 filed 30 September 2026 and Amendment No. 1 filed 9 November 2026 (Securities and Exchange Commission filing index for Trinzic, filer 0002101664, checked 16 November 2026: no later amendment); Trinzic board named 9 November 2026; investor days 11 and 12 November 2026. Still open as of 16 November 2026: record date, distribution ratio (pro-forma assumes one Trinzic share per two KBR shares), the roughly $1.7 billion Trinzic financing (no financing 8-K filed by KBR through 12 November 2026), Form 10 effectiveness, NYSE listing approval, the tax ruling and the board's declaration. Next dated checkpoint: Trinzic 2027 guidance in February 2027.
forcing_function: 4 January 2027, when KBR holders receive Trinzic shares and each half must be priced against its own peer group instead of as one conglomerate at about 6.55 times earnings. Three gates come first, each observable: (1) launch and pricing of Trinzic's roughly $1.7 billion of notes and term loans and the roughly $1.68 billion cash payment to KBR, which is a legal precondition; (2) a further Form 10 amendment carrying the record date and distribution ratio, then effectiveness and NYSE listing approval - the record date should appear by about mid-to-late December, and its absence by about 18 December 2026 is the clearest early warning of a slip; (3) the KBR board's declaration of the distribution. After the split, two slower forces: forced selling of Trinzic in January-February 2027 by holders and index funds that did not choose it, and KBR's sale of its 19.9% Trinzic stake within about twelve months, which deleverages the retained KBR below about one times.
consensus_delta:
Where we disagree with the market has narrowed, and it is now about multiples, not facts. Before the investor days the street's parts work largely assumed retained KBR would earn $460-500 million; the published standalone baseline is about $425 million, and the stock fell 9% in two days to reflect it. We accept the lower number - our own parts value falls from about $51 to about $46.

The disagreement that remains: at $35.67 the market is paying almost exactly the value of the outcome in which the split happens and neither half re-rates (Trinzic at 7 times, retained KBR at 8 times, about $35). That treats a 10%-growth, 12%-margin, under-one-times-levered licensing and advisory business as if it were a plain engineering contractor, and treats Trinzic at the bottom of a government-services range that already de-rated by about four turns since mid-2024. We think the market has over-corrected on the investor-day disclosures: it priced the disappointment fully and is giving away the probability that either half trades near its own peers. The consensus price target of about $45 (eight covering analysts, pre-investor-day) is close to our parts value, which suggests the street still believes the arithmetic even as the tape doubts it.
valley_of_death:
The risky window is the seven weeks to 4 January 2027 plus the six to eight weeks after it. No funding cliff: liquidity about $1.1 billion, group net leverage 2.1 times against a 2.5 times ceiling, dividend declared 14 October 2026.

Four things sit in the window. First, the Trinzic debt offering, about $1.7 billion for a company with falling 2027 revenue and 3.15 times net leverage at launch; a wide print or postponement reads straight through to the date. Second, the record date: if no Form 10 amendment with a record date and ratio appears by about 18 December 2026, assume the date is slipping. Third, the first weeks of separate trading in January-February 2027, when forced sellers of Trinzic and KBR's own announced stake sale weigh on the new shares and therefore on the combined value a KBR holder owns. Fourth, February 2027: Trinzic's first 2027 guidance (management has already flagged "a modest growth year") and KBR's fourth-quarter cash flow, which must deliver $190-230 million to hit the $560-600 million full-year adjusted operating cash flow guide.
positioning_washout:
Most of the forced selling comes after the event, not before. On 4 January 2027 every KBR holder receives Trinzic shares - about 63 million on the assumed one-for-two ratio - in a levered, 83%-federal services company they owned KBR largely to avoid; index funds will re-sort both lines and sweep out small residual positions regardless of value. On top of that, KBR now intends to sell its 19.9% Trinzic stake (about 15.7 million shares on the assumed ratio) "within approximately 12 months, subject to market conditions," which is a faster and more visible block of supply than the five-year window in the Form 10.

Before the event there is some sign the washout has already started in the parent: a 9% fall on two to three times normal volume across the two investor days, taking the shares to roughly the no-re-rate value. That is a style-and-information sell-off, not mechanical forced selling. The practical read: own the parent now for the split, and keep a tranche for Trinzic shares in January-February 2027 when the forced selling lands.
moderator_conclusion:
Buy at today's price, sized as a firm but not maximum position, and keep a tranche for the forced selling in Trinzic shares after 4 January 2027.

The date is fixed and close: the split into retained KBR and Trinzic is set for 4 January 2027, restated by both companies at their investor days on 11 and 12 November 2026. The investor days also brought bad news on the numbers - retained KBR earns about $425 million on a fully loaded standalone basis rather than the $460 million or more the market had assumed, and Trinzic launches at 3.15 times net leverage into a NASA headwind - and the stock fell 9% in two days. We have marked our own parts value down accordingly, from about $51 to about $46. But the price fell further than the value did. At $35.67 the shares sit almost exactly on what the two halves are worth if the split happens and neither is re-rated (about $35), and only about 7.5% above the roughly $33 the conglomerate is worth if the split slips. Upside to the parts value is about 29%; the probability-weighted base case is about $40. That is close to 4 to 1.

This is a four, not a five, for three reasons. There is no contractual floor: a spin-off is not a takeover, and the $33 figure is a judgement about a multiple, corroborated by May 2026 insider buying at $30.60-32.47 but not guaranteed. Nothing is legally committed yet: the record date, ratio and financing are still blank, and KBR can pull the transaction even if every condition is met. And the first weeks after the split carry predictable selling pressure on Trinzic - now including KBR's own plan to sell its 19.9% stake within a year - which a KBR holder owns from day one.

Re-underwrite immediately if no record date is announced by about 18 December 2026, if Trinzic's debt offering prices wide or is postponed, or if February 2027 guidance comes in below the investor-day frameworks. Correction to our own board record: the catalyst entry still carries this event as undated with a target of $53 dated 8 June 2026; it should be re-dated to 4 January 2027 with the target cut to about $46 and the floor kept near $33.
interrogator_dossier:
# KBR, Inc. - Interrogator dossier (event-driven special situation)

Prepared 16 November 2026. Share price used throughout: $35.67 (live quote, 16 November 2026; Friday 13 November closed at $35.59). KBR has 126.1 million shares outstanding, a market value of about $4.50 billion, and a 52-week range of $29.94 to $45.37.

This is a judgement on one event, not on KBR as a business to own forever: the planned separation of KBR's government-services arm into a new New York Stock Exchange company called Trinzic (ticker TZIC), targeted for 4 January 2027. The questions are whether the event is real, whether the date is firm, and what catches the share price if the event disappoints.

## What changed since the last review (9 November 2026)

Two things, and they pull in opposite directions.

First, the information event happened and it disappointed the market. KBR held its investor day on 11 November and Trinzic on 12 November 2026 in New York, publishing standalone figures for the first time. The stock fell from $38.90 (10 November close) to $36.29 on 11 November (down 6.7%) and to $35.32 on 12 November (down a further 2.7%), on roughly two to three times normal volume. Two days of new standalone disclosure took about 9% off the bundle.

Second, the date got firmer. Both management teams restated 4 January 2027 at their own events, and Trinzic's chief executive called the separation "on track." That is now seven weeks away.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

KBR announced on 24 September 2025 that it would split in two, under the headline "Expected to be Completed Mid-to-Late 2026." That first timetable was missed: completion was reset to 4 January 2027 (the first business day of KBR's 2027 fiscal year) in August 2026 and has held since. Since then every stated step has landed on time: the name Trinzic (30 July 2026), a chief financial officer designate (Nicholas Veasey, 1 July 2026), a chief executive designate (Michael LaRouche, 24 September 2026), the registration statement every American spin-off must file - a Form 10 - on 30 September 2026, its first amendment on 9 November 2026 (confirmed on the Securities and Exchange Commission's filing index for Trinzic, filer 0002101664; no further amendment has been filed as of 16 November), the eight-person Trinzic board on 9 November, and both investor days on 11-12 November.

The business story is a deliberate split of fortunes. The retained KBR keeps the faster-growing process-technology and advisory business; Trinzic takes the larger, slower government-services business together with most of the new borrowing.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Separation on track for 4 January 2027 | Restated by both companies on 11-12 November; every dated step since August 2026 has landed. Record date, distribution ratio and financing still not announced. | Supported, not yet committed |
| Retained KBR is a growth company | Standalone 2026 revenue about $2.90 billion; target of 10% or more organic revenue growth a year from 2026 to 2029 (to about $3.85 billion), adjusted EBITDA margin of 12% or more, free cash flow conversion of 85% or more. These are stated as objectives, not guidance. | Plausible, unproven |
| Retained KBR earning power | Standalone accounting baseline of about $425 million of adjusted earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (adjusted EBITDA) - built from the segment's roughly $550 million, less $107 million of allocated corporate and shared cost and an $18 million pension item. 2027 target "more than $425 million" despite a roughly $100 million headwind as a liquefied-natural-gas joint venture winds down. Standalone corporate cost about $55 million a year. | Lower than the market assumed |
| Trinzic is a steady compounder | Last-twelve-month revenue about $5.1 billion and adjusted EBITDA $483 million (9.5% margin); adjusted EBITDA $357 million (2023), $400 million (2024), $444 million (2025). Targets: 3-6% annual revenue growth excluding NASA insourcing, margin of 9% or more, more than $700 million of cumulative operating cash flow after interest over three years. NASA bringing work in-house costs about $200 million, or about 4%, of 2027 revenue; 2027 described as "a modest growth year," with formal guidance in February. | Steady, not growing |
| Trinzic leverage is manageable | Net leverage at separation about 3.15 times adjusted EBITDA (about $1.52 billion of net debt), to be brought to 2.5 times or below from cash flow; debt reduction is the stated first priority, dividend to be revisited in 12-24 months. | Heavier than the 3.0 times modelled last week |
| Group guidance intact | Full-year 2026 guidance reaffirmed on 29 October 2026: revenue $7.90-8.36 billion, adjusted EBITDA $980 million to $1.04 billion, adjusted earnings per share $3.87-4.22. | Supported |

The key forensic number is the retained company's $425 million baseline. Last week's work assumed about $460 million. The difference is the full allocation of corporate and shared cost plus the joint-venture wind-down, and it is the most likely reason the stock fell on the KBR investor day rather than the Trinzic one.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Confident and specific on the event; careful on the numbers. Both companies framed medium-term figures as objectives, not guidance, and Trinzic deferred 2027 guidance to February. The separation language has moved from aspiration to logistics: standalone systems are live, the board is named, the leadership teams presented separately.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Medium to high. One documented timetable slip (mid-to-late 2026 became 4 January 2027), followed by fifteen months of hitting every stated date. Operating guidance reaffirmed three quarters running, with an earnings beat in the latest quarter. Four insiders bought in the open market in May 2026 between $30.60 (chief financial officer Shad Evans) and $32.47 (director Carlos Sabater).

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- What multiple the retained company earns. At 10.0 times $425 million it is worth about $27 a KBR share; at 8.0 times about $20. That range is most of the uncertainty in the whole situation.
- How fast KBR sells its retained 19.9% of Trinzic. Management now says "within approximately 12 months, subject to market conditions," with proceeds to repay debt, taking net leverage below about one times. That is faster than the five-year window in the Form 10 and creates a disclosed block of Trinzic supply in 2027.
- Trinzic's financing. Roughly $1.7 billion of notes and term loans must be raised and about $1.68 billion paid across to KBR before the split. No financing 8-K had been filed by either company as of 16 November 2026.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

Red flags.
- The investor days lowered the earning-power base: about $425 million for retained KBR against roughly $460 million assumed, and Trinzic at 3.15 times leverage against roughly 3.0 times.
- The market's verdict on the new information was a 9% fall in two days.
- Seven weeks out, the record date, distribution ratio and financing amounts are still blank, and no condition to the distribution has been satisfied. The Form 10 amendment states KBR "has the right to terminate or modify the distribution, even if all of the conditions are satisfied." Nothing here is contractual.
- Trinzic launches with falling revenue (NASA insourcing), about 83% United States federal revenue, and a peer group whose valuation multiples have compressed from about 13 times in mid-2024 to about 9 times.
- A disclosed seller: KBR's 19.9% stake is to be sold within about a year.

Green flags.
- Firm, repeatedly restated date; machinery real (Form 10 amended, listing applied for, board and executives named, systems cut over).
- The bundle now trades at about 6.55 times guided 2026 adjusted EBITDA (enterprise value of about $6.62 billion: $4.50 billion of market value plus $2.12 billion of net debt, on $1.01 billion at the guidance midpoint) - roughly where a disappointed conglomerate would trade.
- Retained KBR leaves with net leverage below two times, falling below about one times after the stake sale, and owns the growing half.
- Liquidity about $1.1 billion; quarterly dividend of 16.5 cents declared 14 October 2026.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The price now sits almost exactly on the value of the "split happens, nobody re-rates" outcome: Trinzic at 7 times $483 million less $1.52 billion of net debt (about $14.75 a KBR share) plus retained KBR at 8 times $425 million less about $0.85 billion of net debt (about $20.20) gives about $35. The market has priced the disappointment and is giving the re-rating away. The capital structure still says what management believes: the debt goes with the shrinking half, the chief executive stays with the growing one, and the stake sale is being accelerated to deleverage the parent.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

The event is real, dated and seven weeks away; management has earned credibility on separation logistics since its one early slip. The floor is not contractual: a spin-off is not a takeover, and nobody owes a holder a price. What backstops the shares if the split slips is the conglomerate's own multiple - about $33 at 6.0-6.5 times guided earnings - corroborated by the May 2026 insider buying at $30.60-32.47 and a 52-week low of $29.94. The new information lowered the parts value, but the price fell further than the parts did, so the gap between price and floor has narrowed from about 15% to about 7.5%.

Moat and secular risk are secondary here. Retained KBR owns a genuine but narrow intangible-asset advantage (more than 85 licensed process technologies); Trinzic has incumbency in federal contracting with shrinking revenue. Narrow and stable overall; the secular pressures (federal procurement squeeze on one side, energy-transition demand on the other) are manageable.
